//: Declarative data for the SCENARIO panel + quest checklist in playground.html. Each entry is keyed by a FILES filename; "__fallback__" covers any file with no entry (e.g. a new blank file the visitor created). Loaded at runtime by loadScenarios() — see the check-name vocabulary documented there.

demo.md.body: Start here. This is the smallest possible VisiMark document — one vmark block computing a total from a table.

quest.text: Change a Qty or Price cell and watch Knowledge update
Switch to the Knowledge tab and find the new total
Click Infer anyway, just to see what it says about a document that's already annotated

example-invoice.md.body: A fully-worked, fully-verified invoice: line items, VAT, an early-payment schedule, and a currency conversion, all cross-checked against each other. Every bold number in Preview is backed by a formula, not typed by hand.

quest.text: Change a Qty or Rate cell and watch every total recompute
Open Reasoning to see the dependency order

example-invoice-drift.md.body: The same invoice as above, except someone hand-edited a number after the fact, a date got typed in the wrong format, and a formula call itself in a circle — a small catalogue of everything `check` is built to catch.

quest.text: Open Build and run it — watch it come back red, cell by cell
Edit anything to trigger fmt — the stale numbers snap back in line, though the date and the circular formula still need a human

example-quote-plain.md.body: A quote with real numbers in real tables — but no VisiMark formulas at all. This is the adoption story: most documents start out exactly like this.

quest.text: Click Infer — VisiMark proposes the rules it thinks produced these numbers
Watch Knowledge fill in with real computed values

example-charts.md.body: Two charts — a bar chart and a pie chart — rendered as SVG directly from the tables above them, not pasted in from another tool.

quest.text: Edit a Revenue or Cost cell and watch the bar chart regenerate
Open Reasoning and find the `chart` declaration

example-executable-documentation.md.body: A Kubernetes capacity budget where the headline number — the maximum worker-node count — is derived from cost, node price, and a reserved-capacity percentage, not typed in by whoever last edited the doc.

quest.text: Open Knowledge to see eval's structured output
Change the worker node's monthly cost and watch `MaxNodes` recompute

__fallback__.body: A blank file — nothing to demonstrate yet.

quest.text: Write a table with a `vmark` block under it and watch Knowledge fill in
Or paste in a plain table with no formulas and click Infer
